text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd One day I'm gonna miss the fum little prisons that keep our little one out of harms way, but until that day, I love this little crate for children.

It's nothing revolutionary--hell, after my St Bernard grew tired of his crate I thought--damn, this would be great for children. Apparently someone else thought that, and from the likes of what's out there, a few others did as well. Anyway, we've evolved to the point where decorative monsters and fun colors make it seem more humane and fun and less "now I have my hands free to drink a beer" (note that I do not use this to support my drinking habits, as I'm ok with kids crawling on the dirt while I drink--I just hate doing added laundry). The monsters seem to amuse me more than junior, but perhaps that says something about the dark voices I hear rather than the artistic merits of the designers. I appreciate them nonetheless. The collapsing and folding bit is nice, so we can take it to family day at the demolition derby or one of those bikini car washes. The "sets up in under 1 minute" is true, but it's even quicker if you do it yourself (junior is still working on the hand-eye coordination) and you put down the beer. Best of all--the wheels! Why fold it up and take up all the space in your car for a car seat, when you can tie this to the back of the family truckster and give junior a chance to enjoy the great outdoors while you drive! The comprehensive padding (and bouncy floor) will come in handy when junior joins the toddler wrestling set, and future WWE fortunes will easily cover the modest investment in this play yard.

In all honestly, this is a nice play set. No kids gets were harmed, neglected, or otherwise in need of CPS. Have a great day.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217) If your kids primarily want this kit because, "cool, I made my own stickers!" then they probably will enjoy it. If, like me, they liked the look of the stickers in the advertising, be warned that's more difficult to achieve. I included some pictures of my finished stickers to give an idea of the type of stickers included.

Update: In the end, I've found it easiest to put the drops of paint directly on the sticker sheet, with the desired colors in the right spots (including a red and yellow drop together to make orange, or two red and one blue to make purple, or two yellow and one blue to make green. The blue is very strong and tends to overwhelm the other colors, so use less of it). THEN I use the roller (included) or a sponge brush (not included) to mix the colors directly on the sticker. The problem with using the mat as directed is that too much paint made the roller not mix well, but too little paint meant that the stickers didn't evenly coat with the paint. There would be bare spots (even if paint was under that area) or the paint was thin in spots.

Original review: The first thing I did when I got this set was open it and read the directions. Knowing that practice makes perfect, I tried my first efforts on some white card stock. I followed the directions about the amount of paint to drop on the mat and how many times to run the roller over those drops. The roller started skidding instead of rotating after two passes, so the paint wasn't mixing in the cool, tie-dye-look way. As I used all three colors, the paint quickly turned into a muddy, grayed color. I put the card stock down on the paint, rubbed on the card stock to transfer the paint, turned it over and used the Pattern Design Tool to scratch some lines into the solid color. Some paint came off, some didn't, so it wasn't a clean plaid-pattern type look. Hmm. I looked at the pictures more closely and realized you use the pattern tool on the paint BEFORE you transfer the paint to the paper. The transfer mat looked so much like the finished notebook that this wasn't as clear as it could have been, and the text didn't mention this information. Ok, so that worked, though it's a little hit-or-miss how nice it'll look.

Next attempt: The paint pattern turned into a variety of greens again rather than a tie-dye look, but I loaded the roller (like the cover of the directions shows) and rolled it over the stencil of the dots. Not one bit of paint got on the card stock below the stencil. I used a sponge-brush to pick up paint and dab it on the card stock through the stencil. That worked, but the sponge brush isn't included in this set. I mixed more paint and I used the roller on the zebra stripes stencil, and just a little got through in the larger portions of the design. I tried flipping the paint-covered stencil and rubbing the paint on the stencil onto the card. That worked pretty well, but it's not quite as nice of a design. Then I realized I'd mixed up the directions. You either press the stencil into the paint on the transfer mat and transfer that to the card stock OR put the stencil on the transfer mat, put the paint on the stencil, then roll it down through the holes in the stencil onto the transfer mat, and finally transfer it to the card stock. The roller is only for mixing the paint.

Next try: I only used yellow and red paint and less of it, and I finally got a pretty yellow, orange, and red tie-dye look. If I put a sticker from the sticker sheet down on the paint and rubbed to transfer the paint, that would be a decent success. But I put the card stock on the paint and rubbed the paint onto the card stock. It looked pretty good, but some spots had less paint than others.

So (1) practice a bit before you do your stickers, (2) use only two colors at a time if you wish to create brighter colors (less gray or brownish areas), and (3) you may be able to use 6-9 drops of paint, but this made the roller just skid for me; fewer drops resulted in better blending. Putting the drops in groups (several drops of the same color next to each other) rather than alternately (blue, then yellow, then red) also resulted in more colorful mixes.

Clean up is easy--simply run the mat and tools under warm water in your sink, then dry with a paper towel. All materials are nontoxic. The paints may stain clothing or furniture, though, so wear protective clothing when working with the paint, cover the work surface while painting, and wash up immediately with warm water when finished.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217)

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

There are (at least) 3 different ways to build the top row that  all seem correct. But then you move on to the second row, which is also mono-color(ish) and suffers from the same issue. So you find out that the top row is all wrong based on how the second row doesn't fit. So then you move onto the 3rd row - where the patterned pieces start AND THAT DOESN"T FIT WITH THE TOP TWO ROWS. So you end up rebuilding the second row based on the third row and the top row based on the now-reconstructed second row. It was maddening. Really, make it tough but only one solution please. Otherwise a very enjoyable puzzle and I'd definitely buy this brand again,

NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case I didn't expect this drone to be so tiny but no matter. It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

What I enjoy about this is that it is easy to fly and the instruction manual was fairly easy to understand. It is small and lightweight so won't really injure somebody if it happens to crash land on somebody.

The drone itself has an extra set of blades in case the blades that are already on it get broken, as well as extra batteries for the drone itself. It even comes with a screw driver so you can open the battery compartments. This way no hunting down your own tools.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Firestrike This is my first external cocking blaster and I'm in awe of its range and accuracy.  Flat, in the house shots, are going from my kitchen, down the hall, and thru the family room and hitting the wall (45 feet!).  This is by far as well as my Rampage does. Accuracy is also superb.  I wasn't sure that such little cocking force was going to be able to shoot darts so far or fast.  This little gem will fire elite darts and whistlers.  It does not like streamlines and the suction cup darts.  The bullseye LED target light works pretty good in the dark, and seem to be accurate enough to nail a human size target at 30 feet.  I love the way the 2 spare dart holders seem to blend into the overall scheme of the blaster. The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Chutes and Ladders Board Game Like many of us over 40, we grew up with this game and recognize the graphics of the Classic Chutes and Ladders Board Game. Recently, after my dad passed, we cleared out our old house and found my old game. It followed my brother home to his family, but now I'm curious to compare the two.

Outside of nostalgia, the question is if the game stands on its own in 2015. My four year-old boy thinks so. He doesn't care about 1972 (or even know it existed, as time began with him, as he sees it). He begs to play it, right along with Trouble! and Legos.

Essentially, there's no strategy. The person going version has a small chance of winning, but for all intents and purposes, it is pure chance.

To move forward, the player spins from 1-6. Whatever square he might land on is either neutral, a ladder or a slide. Slides move him back to an earlier square, ladders move him up, and neutral squares allow him to stay put until the next move. There is no decision making.

Is it fun? Very much so, according to my boy. As there are 100 squares, there are plenty of opportunities to climb ladders and slide down. It is a little tricky to follow which direction to go, as the numbers start left-to-right, but zig-zag at each end. A patient older child or adult needs to be on-hand to help with game play.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Chutes and Ladders Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

text_fidelity_a:
My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike [[VIDEOID:4ac7ba54c290a47a623bdcdbf7740f53]] This is an excellent My Little Pony doll and puppy. At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form
-Twilight Sparkle can't stand on her own, but this is typical for dolls like this

Hasbro Gaming Scrabble Crossword Game What you have here is one fine game. Classic, traditional, great for all ages.

Know a bunch of words? Short ones? Long ones? Skinny ones? Know any big fat words you just can't use anywhere else? Use them here. Show off how big your vocabulary is, and that you know how to use it. Of course, there are rules about which ones count, but mostly, regular words are OK. Just nothing with capitals or foreign words, unless of course, you are from somewhere else, but then, they aren't foreign any longer, are they?

Order up a serving of Scrabble. Figure out if you need this version or the deluxe version (which is mighty cool.) If you are new to Scrabble, this is the version to start with.

When you get the game in the mail, call up some friends, turn on some tunes, crack open something tasty and cold, and start munching a few chips. This ain't a game you gotta be smart to play. I've seen guys who only know small words, but they could see the best ways to use them. Vocabs don't win the game. Thinking on your feet will win the game.

I fully recommend Scrabble.

text_fidelity_a:
PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla) I also tried the chocolate version of this donut kit and was quite disappointed in the taste of the donuts. This vanilla option is much better. In anticipation of less than ideal taste I added some good quality vanilla extract which also helped boost the flavor.

Still, the issues I had with the chocolate version are also present in this version. The box it comes in is cheap and flimsy, and dented up quite a bit in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla)

text_fidelity_a:
Stemnex Amazing Steam Engine I would recommend this one more for older children and teenagers because there is over 100 parts here and it may be a bit too challenging for younger kids. Regardless, this is one of the neatest things ever. Kids who love trains will definitely love this. I am reminded of something my dad helped me build for a science fair project when I was in 4th grade, and I won a blue ribbon. The one I had though was made from metal parts and springs and such that he put together from old carburators and such. It looked very much like this one. Working on this made me think of my dad when we built my science project. So this would be perfect, in my honest opinion, for any parents to work on with their kids. You just might make some cool memories. It may also be a good item for kids who are home-schooled and learning about this kind of thing in science.

As for product attributes, the pieces go together easily and the instructions are pretty easy to follow. I recommend possibly not taking the pieces off of the brackets until they are needed, this way they won't get lost. The box is quite large, but just the right size to store away under a bed or raised sofa.
text_fidelity_b: Stemnex Amazing Steam Engine

This marble maze series made by Hape is tremendous. We have had so much fun building with this. Not only does each set come with a book and great step by step directions with photos for making multiple mazes the color coded-functionality of the transporting blocks help kids work out marble flow and direction when building on their own. Some blocks allow marbles to flow one or two directions or alternating directions as well as some being travel though pieces while others are drop into pieces.

Although the wood pieces fit together they do not lock so it can be knocked over which may be an issue for younger children who get really excited like my four year old grandson but my seven year old son builds and maintains his mazes with no problems.

It also comes with a bag full or marbles so never having a marble should never be an issue. We use a funnel and just load the maze up and it can have a marble flow continuously for as long as someone collects and loads. It's a bundle of excitement and engages the kids for HOURS!

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad

text_fidelity_a:
Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers I absolutely love the concept of this little worker placement game, but the execution is not great.

You spend each turn doing basic worker placement stuff - go here, get resources, then convert those resources somewhere else, all while building a cell wall around your plant cell in an effort to turn your stuff into points. There is real science here - you use different cell components according to the actual chemical formulas of 6 water + 6CO2 to do photosynthesis, and cards are named after actual scientific stuff. There's also an area control segment of the board where you can earn some minor points and bonuses. The highlight, though, is that when you play this game, you'll know more about real-life science than when you started, and that's a pretty cool thing.

The game suffers though, because there just isn't much to do at the end of the game, and catching up is extremely difficult given that so few actions lead to points, and so many of the things you can collect are useful for only one or two functions. It's a little bit like saying that the science got in the way of the fun. When one person does the action to trigger the end of the game, there is usually a rush to do the singular action left that can generate points, and if you don't have it, you just stockpile some useless resources. That's a poor endgame, and on second or third playthoughs, you'll find that there are really only one or two viable strategies for winning at all.

Ultimately, this is an awesome game for teaching a small group of teenage scientists more about cell structures, but at the price of a hobby board game, it's tough to put in the hands of teachers for classroom use, and harder still to spend valuable class time to educate non-gamers about the intricacies of worker placement prior to their first play. And that play will run the course of a class period, more or less, so that has it's benefits, and it's detriments.

As a gamer's game, we found the concept extremely interesting, but the execution needed a little work. It won't hit the table often, because every other worker placement game we have is more exciting at the endgame, and offers us a greater variety of strategies for winning.

Do note that the addition of the "Mangrove" board, which was a kickstarter stretch goal, is essential to me keeping this one in our collection. The normal board is not nearly as good.
text_fidelity_b: Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist Electronic Scrabble Twist is a great idea and it more like an electronic version of Boggle in which players can make as many three, four, or five letter words as possible from a random group of letters before time runs out. Simply press the buttons on the unit to spell the words and “twist” to save the word - the bigger the word, the more points you receive for that word. Unfortunately, I love the idea more than the execution. There are both good and bad features of the game, which I’ve summarized below.

Good:
• Games are quick and rules are basic
• The game can be played by anywhere from 1 to 8 players, depending on the game mode
• There are different games that can be played and different levels of difficulty with varying lengths of the time players are given to find words
• The game quickly shuts off automatically if not in use
• The letters will automatically display in the right direction even if the unit is turned, which is good for the party mode in which the unit is passed and also means it works well for both left and right handed players
• The Turbo mode, for head-to-head play between two or more players is fun
• The sound can be turned off for quieter play

Not So Good:

• The worst part of the game is that the letters are hard to read and is a strain on your eyes after playing for a while. People in my family of all age groups said the same thing.
• Three AA batteries are required, but they’re not included
• The instructions on using the game unit aren’t clear (I was able to figure out how to use it by playing the game a few times.)
• The solo mode tracks high scores, but not by name. It doesn’t feel like you’re working toward anything since you can’t really compare scores from game to game since it depends on the letters you had for each game.
• When the sound is on, it’s loud, even at the lowest level. Different sounds do alert you that you’ve played a valid word. A second sound plays if the word you’ve played is invalid or a duplicate. Sounds also let you know if time is about to run out, but I found that this distracted me from finding my final words
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist
